title: Fenwick and Segment Trees
summary: Answering range questions on changing arrays - prefix sums and their weakness, the Fenwick (binary indexed) tree with its lowest-set-bit trick for O(log n) updates and prefix sums, segment trees for any associative operation such as minimum or maximum, building, point updates and range queries, and a first look at lazy propagation for range updates.

cards.q: What is the lowest set bit of 12 (binary 1100)?
cards.a:
4

12 & -12 = 4: the rightmost 1 is in the 4s place.

cards.q: Why can't a Fenwick tree answer range-minimum queries the way it answers range sums?
cards.a:
A minimum cannot be subtracted away

A range sum is prefix(r) - prefix(l - 1). The prefix trick needs an inverse operation, which min does not have.

cards.q: In a segment tree for range sums, what should a query return for a segment that does not overlap [l, r]?
cards.a:
0

The identity of addition, so it does not change the combined result.
